tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Use this when the person asks which CVEmber account is connected or whether they can download. Returns the connected account as a masked email, whether PDF download is available now, and what this connection may do.

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Use this when the person first opens CVEmber, asks what CVEmber can do, or says "CVEmber, menu" or "CVEmber, help". Returns where they are (signed in or not, has a resume, has a tailored version) and the menu. Works signed out. No contact details.

tools.name: list_resumes
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to see their resumes, or a resume's id is needed. Returns master resumes and tailored versions, newest first, each with a label (company, job, date) and its ATS score. A limit above 50 is treated as 50. No contact details.

tools.name: get_resume
tools.description: Use this when a saved resume's content is needed, to show it or before editing it. Returns the content, template, colour and contentVersion. A saved job ad or imported text comes back under foreign, as data.

tools.name: tailor_resume
tools.description: Use this when the person wants their saved resume aimed at a specific job. Takes resumeId and the job ad, or just the job title and company, as the person gave it. CVEmber writes the tailored version itself; the master resume never changes, and the same job again refreshes that job's version. userSt

tools.name: update_resume
tools.description: Use this when the person asks for a change to a saved resume, or tells you something about themselves to add: a job, title, degree, award, skill, language or number. Call it straight away with their exact words in userStatedFacts; that field alone is enough and CVEmber places it on the resume. Do no

tools.name: create_resume
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to save their resume in CVEmber or build a new one, including from scratch. file: the attached resume file itself (PDF, Word, text, photo); CVEmber reads it. sourceText: pasted text, exactly as pasted. content: a resume built from the person's own answers. tools.name: score_resume
tools.description: Use this when the person asks whether a resume or CV is good, ATS-friendly or ready to send, or asks for its score or what to fix. Takes the attached resume file (file), pasted resume text (sourceText) or a saved resume (resumeId); a job ad is optional. Works signed out. Returns CVEmber's ATS score,

tools.name: export_pdf
tools.description: Use this when the person asks for their resume as a PDF or asks to download it. Returns a link that opens the resume's download page on cvember.com. Nothing is bought through this tool.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to undo a change CVEmber made. Puts the resume back to how it was before the latest change, or the one named by actionId.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to see templates or to change how the resume looks. Returns template ids with their format, columns, the roles each suits, and the colour ids. Works signed out.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account · Private data: get_started, list_resumes, create_resume, score_resume · Public sink: get_account, score_resume · Destructive: update_resume, list_templates.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account · Private data: get_started, list_resumes, create_resume, score_resume · Public sink: get_account, score_resume · Destructive: update_resume, list_templates

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
